title: A Plea: Stop Building and Sharing IP Infringing Projects. Please.
author: AsparagusOk8818
selftext:
...This will likely fall on deaf ears, but I figure I may as well try: 

You guys doing this are going to ruin a lot of the experience for everyone, including yourselves. I know the thought process here is something like, 'lol, the technology can't be stopped, there's nothing the big companies can do about this!' 

People just ripping-off songs on Suno thought the same thing.

Now Suno is effectively controlled by WMG and Sony after Suno settled a lawsuit with them.   
  
  
The technology can't be stopped, but it can be entangled with and poisoned by big companies. Suno went from 'make what you want, share it, download it, whatever' to '20 downloads a month, here is a long list of the ways you are restricted in sharing or using music produced with Suno'. Because people wouldn't stop jusrt fckn copying Maroon 5 and Taylor Swift songs over and over again for God knows what reason.  


Your 'cool' Spider-Man or DBZ one-shot game? It's garbage. It's a bad game whose sole function is to be used as part of a tapestry in a lawsuit by Disney or Square Enix or Bandai Namco or who-the-fuck-ever against the LLMs we are all using. And it'll be the same story as Suno - suddenly there's a huge moat around capability and you're just NOT ALLOWED anymore.   


I'd also beg the mods of this sub if they ever see this to please consider banning, very specifically, IP-infringing 'one-shot' garbage, to discourage people from making it.

replies.author: IDreamtOfManderley
replies.body: Yes it is. Derivative works are fan works. If someone makes a DBZ game for free, that is a derivative work, it is a fan game and it is fair use as long as it is not monetized. What are you talking about. Fair use is a grey area in the lawand thus it can be ignored or work on shaky ground, but it could be used to protect such a game as long as no money is being made. The organization for transformative works exists to advocate for this law.  Whether someone can afford to use the defence rather than just comply with a takedown request, or a platform complies for you is another story. Forced compliance by a corporation on behalf of another corporation is not the same as a legal enforcement.
